key_insight: Random intermittent jet forcing can drive mixing at a salt-stratified interface, and at large density jumps the interface can sharpen even while irreversible mixing still occurs.
engineering_relevance: The results inform how heterogeneous, bursty forcing may transport and restructure stratified fluids in environmental and industrial mixing systems.
method: Two-layer salt-stratified fluid experiment forced by a randomly actuated synthetic jet array (RASJA).
Interface evolution measured with light attenuation to resolve density-field changes.
Compared interface motion and sharpening across different density jumps and linked changes to background potential energy.
evidence_signal: Measurements show interface upward velocity decreases as the density jump increases, and background potential energy indicates irreversible mixing in both regimes.
watch_item: The findings come from laboratory two-layer conditions, so direct scaling to strongly three-dimensional or field-scale stratified flows may require caution.
paper_title: Mixing and sharpening at the interface of a two-layer fluid forced by random jets
